title: Silicon Creations at DAC 2026: Solutions for clocking, SerDes, and sensing in 2nm (and beyond) - Semiwiki
gist: A DAC 2026 booth promo for analog/mixed-signal IP vendor Silicon Creations that nonetheless carries hard business datapoints: SerDes bookings up more than 200% on the back of a TSMC 3nm 32G multi-protocol design win, several customers already in mass production on TSMC 2nm IP in the trailing twelve months, and nearly a dozen customers adopting its new temperature/voltage sensors. The piece also flags node breadth beyond TSMC into Samsung, Intel Foundry and Rapidus.

insights.claim: Silicon Creations' SerDes bookings have risen more than 200%, driven by a single TSMC 3nm 32G multi-protocol design win — evidence that high-speed interface IP demand is inflecting with AI interconnect buildout.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Interface-IP bookings are a leading indicator for advanced-node AI silicon starts; a >200% jump at a mid-size vendor supports the broader SerDes/IP cycle thesis.
insights.quote: SerDes bookings have increased by more than 200% driven by a TSMC 3nm 32G multi-protocol design win
insights.locator: This year, Silicon Creations is celebrating its 20th anniversary

insights.claim: The DAC 2026 SerDes lineup is aimed squarely at AI datacenter interconnect — PCIe, Ethernet and DisplayPort SerDes plus reference clock generator PLLs for 112/224G Ethernet and PCIe5/6/7 PHYs.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: 224G Ethernet and PCIe6/7 IP readiness is the gating item for next-gen scale-up fabrics — track which IP vendors have silicon-proven PHY clocking.
insights.locator: Visit Silicon Creations at DAC 2026 — this year at DAC, Silicon Creations will highlight

insights.claim: Die-to-die PLLs for UCIe PHYs are offered from 2nm and above, positioning clocking IP as a chiplet-era attach point rather than a monolithic-SoC commodity.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Chiplet disaggregation creates new per-die IP attach — UCIe-adjacent IP suppliers get more content per system, not less.
insights.locator: Die-to-die PLLs for UCIe PHYs from 2nm and above

insights.claim: Several Silicon Creations customers moved to mass production with TSMC 2nm IP in the trailing 12 months, a concrete third-party datapoint that TSMC 2nm is already carrying production volume rather than only risk starts.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Independent confirmation of N2 ramp timing feeds TSMC revenue-mix and advanced-node pricing models.
insights.quote: In the trailing 12 months alone, several Silicon Creations customers have moved to mass production with their TSMC 2nm IP.
insights.locator: This year, Silicon Creations is celebrating its 20th anniversary

insights.claim: The company's jitter-optimized all-digital-loop LC PLL is now available at 2nm on Samsung and 3nm on TSMC and Intel, indicating third-party IP is being ported across all three leading-edge foundries rather than TSMC alone.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: IP availability is a prerequisite for foundry customer wins — multi-foundry porting is an early tell that Samsung and Intel Foundry are drawing real external designs.
insights.quote: All-digital loop control, jitter-optimized LC PLL, now available from 2nm (Samsung) and 3nm (TSMC, Intel) up to 22nm (GF)
insights.locator: Visit Silicon Creations at DAC 2026 — bullet list

insights.claim: Silicon Creations reports general IP development growing not only on TSMC GAAFET advanced nodes but also at Samsung, Intel Foundry and Rapidus, putting Japan's Rapidus alongside established leading-edge foundries in a commercial IP roadmap.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Rapidus appearing in a commercial IP vendor's active roadmap is an early credibility signal for the Japanese leading-edge effort — watch for follow-on IP and EDA enablement announcements.
insights.quote: General IP developments continue to grow not only in TSMC (GAAFET) advanced nodes but also in Samsung, Intel Foundry, and Rapidus.
insights.locator: This year, Silicon Creations is celebrating its 20th anniversary

insights.claim: Nearly a dozen customers have adopted Silicon Creations' new temperature and voltage sensors, and the sensor IP spans TSMC 2nm through 28nm with further node expansion underway — a new product line converting quickly.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: On-die thermal/voltage sensing is becoming mandatory content as AI silicon power density rises — a structurally growing IP category to track.
insights.quote: nearly a dozen customers have adopted our new temperature (and voltage) sensor(s)
insights.locator: This year, Silicon Creations is celebrating its 20th anniversary

insights.claim: Dynamic frequency scaling with step times under 1ns is being marketed as a headline capability, reflecting that power-management agility, not just peak frequency, is now the differentiator in AI and mobile SoCs.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Sub-nanosecond DFS supports power-capped AI accelerator designs — a spec to compare against competing clocking IP vendors.
insights.locator: Dynamic Frequency Scaling solutions with step times of < 1ns

insights.claim: Silicon Creations claims the majority of the world's top 50 IC companies as customers, with over 2,000 chip designs containing its IP, a portfolio of over 800 unique IP products, more than 150 production tape-outs annually and over 550 customers globally.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Scale metrics for a private analog IP vendor set the benchmark for comparable licensing businesses and any eventual M&A valuation.
insights.quote: The majority of the world’s top 50 IC companies work with Silicon Creations. Over 2,000 chip designs contain the company’s IP, drawn from a portfolio of over 800 unique IP products.
insights.locator: Key takeaways — The majority of the world's top 50 IC companies

insights.claim: Silicon Creations is a privately held IP company founded in 2006, headquartered in Atlanta with engineering in Kraków, Poland, and its silicon-proven analog IP spans 180nm to 2nm — a deliberately foundry-agnostic, node-broad model.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Foundry-agnostic analog IP is a hedge on any single foundry's node success — relevant if leading-edge share shifts among TSMC, Samsung and Intel.
